arguments.name: Lowe’s subject and intentional-causation model
bridge_principles: Identity criteria for a subject differ from criteria for its changing body or parts.
The relevant decision and ramifying neural aggregate have different counterfactual profiles.
arguments.conclusion: On those commitments, distinct subjects can explain intentional action while physical event chains remain complete.
arguments.strongest_objection: A physically sufficient event also fixes that it occurs; relabeling the intentional explanandum as a fact does not by itself remove competing sufficiency. Unity experienced in deciding does not independently settle causal event individuation.
arguments.strongest_reply: Lowe can challenge extension of event closure to facts and distinguish the type of intended outcome from its token realization. This works only with justified distinctions and counterfactuals.
unresolved_issues: Empirical adequacy of the neural/event premises

arguments.name: Bennett’s conditional exclusion challenge
arguments.position: Nonreductive physicalist challenge to dualist compatibility
bridge_principles: Ordinary independent sufficient causes differ from dependent causal descriptions.
Relevant closest-world counterfactuals retain enough background to test genuine causal independence.
arguments.conclusion: A dualist with merely contingent psychophysical links needs a different response than the physicalist dependence strategy, unless a defensible necessitating relation is supplied.
arguments.strongest_objection: The decisive modal test may sever an explanatory embodiment relation and thereby test a different causal situation; metaphysical necessitation is not conceded to physicalism alone.
arguments.strongest_reply: A relation must explain the dependence and have independent motivation; arbitrary covariance cannot be stipulated into the fixed counterfactual background. Bennett also leaves completeness itself as a separate dualist dispute.
unresolved_issues: Coherence and motivation of necessary relations between distinct substances

arguments.name: Engelhardt’s inclusive compatibility reply
arguments.position: Revised substance dualism with dependent property sharing
bridge_principles: Two property bearers need not supply two independently sufficient physical pushes.
Counterfactual comparison should preserve a well-founded explanatory embodiment relation.
arguments.conclusion: A specified substance-dualist variant can contest the inference from two bearers to systematic independent overdetermination.
arguments.strongest_objection: Token sharing and embodiment may merely restate the dependence to be explained; if their modal force is unsupported, exclusion returns. A model that surrenders distinctive independent powers may not meet Lowe’s original explanatory ambition.
arguments.strongest_reply: Require a relation with explanatory standing comparable to relations accepted in physicalist constitution cases; do not assume numerical distinctness entails causal independence.
unresolved_issues: One property instance with multiple bearers
No independently distinctive powers or empirical advantage established
